english.title: Supply registration plate to unregistered supplier
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), supplied

(A)_[a plate]_
(B)_[a device, namely **(..SPECIFY THE DEVICE..),]_
(C)_[an object, namely **(..SPECIFY THE OBJECT..),]_

to an unregistered person, namely **(..SPECIFY THE PERSON..), who was carrying on business which consisted wholly or partly in selling registration plates, and knew or reasonably suspected that it would be used for the purposes of that business (or part of that business) as a registration plate or as part of a registration plate
english.legislation: Contrary to section 29(1) and (2) of the Vehicles (Crime) Act 2001.

english.notes:
(i) Proceedings under this Section instituted by a person or body other than a local authority or a constable must have the permission of the Attorney General.
(ii) See section 20(2) for alternative/additional penalty.
(iii) See section 17(2) for clarification of "carries on business as a registration plate supplier".
(iv) "Registered" means registered in accordance with the provisions of Part 2 of the Vehicles (Crime) Act 2001 in a register established and maintained by the Secretary of State.
(v) See section 31(1) for other interpretations of Part 2 of the Act.

other.penalty:
SUMMARY: A fine not exceeding level five on the standard scale.

NOTE:
Where a registered person is convicted of this offence the court may, instead of or in addition to imposing a fine, by order suspend his registration for any period of up to five years. (section 20(2)).

Time limit for prosecutions:
6 months

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
